about: The epistola of the formulary “Second Sunday after Epiphany” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

s01.translation: Brothers: We have different gifts according to the grace given to us: whether prophecy, let it be according to the rule of faith; or ministry, in ministering; or the one who teaches, in teaching; the one who exhorts, in exhorting; the one who gives, with simplicity; the one who leads, with diligence; the one who shows mercy, with cheerfulness. Let love be without pretense. Hate what is evil; hold fast to what is good. Love one another with brotherly love; take the lead in honoring one another. Do not be sluggish in diligence; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord. Rejoice in hope; be patient in tribulation; persevere in prayer. Share in the needs of the saints; pursue hospitality. Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse. Rejoice with those who rejoice and weep with those who weep. Be of one mind toward one another. Do not set your minds on high things, but agree with the humble.

w002.explanation: The participle opens a sentence that has no main verb in the Latin. It describes us, the faithful, to whom differing gifts of grace are given. No separate word expresses its subject.

w044.explanation: From this word Paul sets out a series of participles without a main verb. Each describes the faithful he addresses and works as an exhortation: hating evil. No separate word expresses their subject, an understood you.

w046.explanation: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): it describes the faithful Paul addresses, cleaving to what is good. No separate word expresses its subject.

w051.explanation: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful Paul addresses are to love one another with brotherly charity. No separate word expresses its subject.

w054.explanation: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to go before one another in showing honor. No separate word expresses its subject.

w057.explanation: The adjective is the predicate of an understood subject, the faithful Paul addresses. The Latin leaves out both the subject and the verb, as throughout the series from “Odiéntes” (w044).

w059.explanation: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful Paul addresses are to be fervent in spirit. No separate word expresses its subject.

w061.explanation: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to serve the Lord. No separate word expresses its subject.

w063.explanation: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to rejoice in hope. No separate word expresses its subject.

w066.explanation: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to bear tribulation patiently. No separate word expresses its subject.

w068.explanation: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to persevere in prayer. No separate word expresses its subject.

w071.explanation: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to share in the needs of the saints. No separate word expresses its subject.

w073.explanation: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to pursue hospitality. No separate word expresses its subject.

w089.explanation: After “Gaudére” (w081) and “flere” (w084), Paul returns to participles: the faithful are to be of one mind toward one another. No separate word expresses their subject, an understood you.

w092.explanation: Like “sentiéntes” (w089), the participle describes the faithful Paul addresses: they are not to set their minds on high things. No separate word expresses its subject.

w095.explanation: Like “sentiéntes” (w089), the participle describes the faithful Paul addresses: they are to consent to the humble. No separate word expresses its subject.
